title: Give third-party plugins their own entry settings and auth service
head: 72eb61692162
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Clean co-merge with open #12996 clears the auth service of an already loaded panel
leads.consequence: A third-party lock/polkit clone that declares a panel and a service is initially given its own auth instance via AuthServiceStore on Loader.onLoaded. With #12996 also merged, syncPluginApis calls reinjectLoadedPanelShellApis on each plugin sync, which unconditionally overwrites item.service with shell.serviceFor(id). Auth services are deliberately absent from _services, so it becomes null and the panel loses its service until a reload. Preserve the AuthServiceStore branch in the reinjection helper as well as onLoaded.

leads.summary: Per-entry snapshot selects the first copy of a duplicate bar-widget ID
leads.consequence: For a third-party allowMultiple widget, or a clone of an allowMultiple built-in, two entries with different inline fields produce the same pluginId-scoped shell facade. findBarLocation returns the first index, so both widgets reading shell.entrySettings see the first widget's settings. Bar.qml still injects each slot's own settings separately, so the new API disagrees with the widget's settings property. Key this API by entry placement/instance, or explicitly document that shell.entrySettings is not per-instance.

leads.summary: Replacement-bar per-entry facade never receives or refreshes entrySettings
leads.consequence: The replacement bar gives its rendered widget pluginShellForBarEntry rather than its full service shell. That facade creates a PluginShellApi with the default empty entrySettings, even if the widget has inline shell.json options; syncPluginApis updates only barConfig, leaving it empty/stale. The new own-entry settings API works only when widgets are under the stock bar, despite the existing settings-update ability of replacement-bar entries.

leads.summary: Open #13064, #13194 and #11079 collide with this change in shell.qml and need intentional conflict resolution
leads.consequence: #13064 moves panel host-API injection into deliverPanelPluginApis and its new helper assigns item.service through serviceFor(id) only. A three-way merge using that PR's own base conflicts in Loader.onLoaded; taking its branch without updating the helper discards this PR's auth service wiring. #13194 conflicts in createScopedPluginShell._serviceLookup; its replacement-bar service policy must be reconciled with this PR's own-auth closure. #11079 also conflicts while replacing createScopedPluginShell's createObject initialization with createPluginApi, so entrySettings must be carried into the new payload if that PR merges. GitHub MERGEABLE on each PR measures their individual base, not pairwise compatibility. #12937 additionally conflicts on AuthServiceStore.get's missing-value return (null versus undefined), although callers here guard with has.

leads.summary: Current quattro tip cannot merge the unchanged PR shell.qml without resolving its panel model conversion
leads.consequence: Current origin/quattro moved panelEntries to a ListModel, including unloadPanels, delegate required properties, connections and finishPluginReload. Merging the pinned PR with that tip produces conflict markers in those regions and in the new pluginEntrySettings/helper region; selecting the PR's old panelEntries branch would undo the base fix. Rebase against the tip and keep its ListModel while transplanting the auth panel assignment. No merged runtime pass can be claimed until resolved.

leads.summary: Added auth-boundary assertions pass when the new settings reader is completely broken
leads.consequence: The changed test greps for assignment wiring but does not exercise pluginEntrySettings, config lookup, deep-copy or live host auth panel wiring. In a sandboxed mutant where pluginEntrySettings always returns {}, all assertions still pass and the runtime section skips without Wayland. Add a config-backed assertion that obtains a scoped API, verifies nested settings and mutation isolation, and checks refresh, rather than matching call text alone.

leads.summary: Shell plugin developer documentation omits the newly exposed entrySettings read API
leads.consequence: Both API-contract sections describe the fields and privileges of the injected third-party shell facade, but neither mentions shell.entrySettings or its JSON-snapshot and id-stripping behaviour. Authors following the documented contract cannot discover the feature or its refresh semantics. Add it next to the inline settings description and note the replacement-bar exception until B2 is fixed.

leads.summary: Nested array shape on first createObject injection is not demonstrated by the new test
leads.consequence: Hypothesis: QML createObject's initial-property conversion may turn arrays nested inside entrySettings into QVariant sequence views or key maps, despite the JSON deep copy; later sync assignment could have a different shape. Open #11079 claims and tests exactly this for adjacent barConfig and manifests and conflicts in createScopedPluginShell. Reproduce in an isolated running Quickshell fixture with an own shell.json entry containing a nested array, assert Array.isArray on first injection and after sync, then either move composite fields to post-creation assignment or drop the concern if identical.

limits: A Wayland compositor was not available in review.py, so the PR's Quickshell runtime fixture skipped; Node/static tests and source-derived probe ran. Hypothesis B8 needs a real Quickshell fixture.

flags.claim: `agents/skills/shell-dev.md` states that "Authentication services must therefore remain outside both `ShellRoot._services` and the host QObject tree."
flags.why: The quote is accurate (shell-dev.md:23), but head still literally satisfies it: auth services go to AuthServiceStore rather than _services (shell.qml:960-964), and they have no QObject parent (createObject(null), shell.qml:950). The exposure goes through JS properties and functions, so an author could reasonably answer that the quoted rule is met. The sentences that are actually violated are shell-dev.md:23 "Do not expose authentication services through new third-party-facing properties" (the panel item's `service`), manual/32-shell-plugins.md:40 "keeping those services outside the reachable host object graph", and the shell.qml:961-963 comment "without adding a traversable property or QObject parent back to the host shell".
flags.fix: Quote manual/32-shell-plugins.md:40 or the shell.qml:961-963 comment instead, or add one of them.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: replaced shell-dev QObject-tree quote with manual/32 'reachable host object graph' and shell-dev 'Do not expose ... third-party-facing properties'

flags.claim: Refusing the fallback only for first-party ids would close the stock path and leave the clone paths open.
flags.why: This is reasoned from source and was not run. It holds only if the refusal checks the installed manifest (shell.pluginRegistry.installedPlugins[id].__isFirstParty). A check on the caller-supplied manifest would not close the stock path, because a forged `{ id }` has no __isFirstParty (shell.qml:761-766). With a clone enabled, resolveEnabledId maps the source id to the third-party clone, so the clone paths stay open.
flags.fix: Optional: "refusing it for ids whose installed manifest is first-party ..."; or keep as is.
flags.disposition: trivial fix applied: 'ids whose installed manifest is first-party'

## What worked

- **Parallel start:** Opus and Sol ran in parallel from one neutral brief.
- **Opus model:** the verbatim-function model made base, old, head and merged comparisons cheap.
- **Sol hunter:** its #12996 interaction lead (B4) was a real, non-obvious issue: a clean textual merge that is semantically broken.
- **Self-check:** it caught seven overstatements, among them a doc quote that the head technically satisfies (D1) and a test suggestion that would miss the keep-id mutant (D2).

## Friction and deviations

- **Coordinator merge-tree during intake:** I ran one `git merge-tree` (default write-tree mode) against the fresh assignment clone `src/`. It writes unreachable objects only, with no ref or worktree change, but it is still a mutation of the clone the reviewers read. Use `git merge-file` on extracted blobs in a scratch directory instead, as done later in `coord-verify/`.
- **GitHub rate limit:** the API limit (shared 5000/hr) was hit during the reviews, mostly by Sol's open-PR search. The freshness recheck waited until reset. `git fetch pull/N/head` works around API limits for source.
- **Sol B7 error:** Sol passed the PR head as the merge base in one `git merge-file` and reported 14 conflicts. The hunter prompt could require recording the three input SHAs per merge.

## Carry forward

- For follow-ups, keep the neutral brief listing the earlier public finding IDs. It made the dispositions direct.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** This follow-up checks head `72eb616` against the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12260#issuecomment-5834271922) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12260#issuecomment-5835081011). The PR was rebased, and its first commit is unchanged from the previously reviewed `70c62cb`. The deep copy resolves the `entrySettings` finding. The authentication-service finding is still present. `pluginServiceFor` no longer returns authentication services, but the fallback moved into facade closures that other `ShellRoot` functions create and cache. Lock and polkit services therefore stay reachable from `ShellRoot`, including on a stock install with no clone.

| Earlier item | Status at `72eb616` |
|---|---|
| Authentication services reachable from `ShellRoot` | Still present, through other paths |
| `entrySettings` shares nested objects with host config | Resolved |
| Note: replacement-bar widgets get no `entrySettings` | Unchanged |

**Verified** (isolated headless model built from verbatim head functions, stub services):

- After a config refresh, `entrySettings` has no `id`, and a nested push no longer changes host config. A nested read-modify-write through `updateEntryInline` now persists. At `70c62cb` it returned `false`.
- `shell.pluginServiceFor(...)` now returns `null` for the lock, polkit and lock-clone ids.
- A lock clone's own facade and its overlay's `service` still return its own authentication service (the #10969 fix). A foreign id still returns `null`.
- The PR's `shell/shell.qml` merges onto current `quattro` without conflicts, and the model gives the same results on that merge.

### Authentication services are still reachable from `ShellRoot`

The author's reply is accurate for `pluginServiceFor`. The `AuthServiceStore` fallback now sits in the `_serviceLookup` and `_firstPartyServiceLookup` closures inside `createScopedPluginShell`. Their `key` and `allowOwnService` come from the arguments of public `ShellRoot` functions. As the earlier review showed, a plugin root without its own `shell` property resolves the bare name `shell` to `ShellRoot`. From there:

| Probe from a plugin without its own `shell` property | Scenario | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shell.pluginServiceFor("omarchy.lock", "omarchy.lock")` | stock | null | null |
| `shell.pluginShellFor({ id: "omarchy.lock" }).serviceFor("omarchy.lock")` | stock | null | **lock service** |
| `shell.createScopedPluginShell({ id: "omarchy.lock" }, "k", true, false).serviceFor("omarchy.lock")` | stock | null | **lock service** |
| `shell.pluginShellForId("user.lockclone").serviceFor("user.lockclone")` | lock clone | null | **clone service** |
| `shell._pluginShellApis["user.lockclone"].serviceFor("user.lockclone")` | lock clone | null | **clone service** |
| `shell.panelLoaders["user.lockclone"].item.service` | lock clone | null | **clone service** |

`shell.pluginShellFor({ id: "omarchy.polkit" }).serviceFor("omarchy.polkit")` returns the polkit service in the same way. The two stock-install rows that return the service at head also returned it at `70c62cb`, so `72eb616` did not introduce them. They are now the main remaining path, and they need no clone.

**Impact:** Unchanged from the earlier review. The lock service exposes `enteredPassword`/`pendingPassword`. Its `finishUnlock()` sets `sessionLock.locked = false` without checking authentication (`shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml`, from source; the call was not run). `manual/32-shell-plugins.md` describes authentication state as protected "by keeping those services outside the reachable host object graph", and `agents/skills/shell-dev.md` says "Do not expose authentication services through new third-party-facing properties."

**Suggested change:** Keep anything that can return an authentication service off every object reachable from `ShellRoot`:
- the facade factories (`pluginShellFor`, `createScopedPluginShell`, `pluginShellForId`);
- the `_pluginShellApis` cache;
- panel items reachable as `panelLoaders[id].item`.

Handing the overlay the raw service always exposes it through `panelLoaders`. The earlier options still apply: keep auth-capable UI inside the service object, as `omarchy.lock` does, or give the overlay a narrow proxy without credential fields or unlock actions. Refusing the fallback only for ids whose installed manifest is first-party would close the stock path and leave the clone paths open. A runtime negative test from a plugin without its own `shell` property could assert that both `shell.pluginServiceFor(authId, authId)` and `shell.pluginShellFor({ id: authId }).serviceFor(authId)` stay `null`. The new assertion only checks that the text of the `pluginServiceFor` body does not mention `AuthServiceStore`.

### Semantic conflict with open #12996

#12996 adds `reinjectLoadedPanelShellApis()`, called from every `syncPluginApis()`, which sets `item.service = shell.serviceFor(id)`. The two PRs merge without a textual conflict, and both PRs' tests pass on the combination. `serviceFor` never returns authentication services, though. In the model, a lock clone overlay's `service` goes from the clone service to `null` after the first sync, both on head plus #12996 and on `quattro` plus both PRs.

**Impact:** This applies only if both PRs land. A lock clone overlay that reads `service`, the pattern from #10969, would lose it on the first plugin sync after loading. An overlay that calls `shell.serviceFor(ownId)` on its own facade keeps working.

**Suggested change:** Whichever PR lands second could have the reinjection leave `service` untouched, or make both injection sites resolve `service` the same way (subject to the authentication suggested change above).

### `entrySettings` notes

**Optional test improvement:** The three new `entrySettings` assertions are text matches. Three mutants of `pluginEntrySettings` each still pass the whole test script: one returns `({})`, one returns the live entry (which brings back the earlier nested-sharing bug), and one keeps `id`. A config-backed check could read a scoped facade's `entrySettings`, assert that it equals the entry without `id`, mutate a nested value and confirm that host config is unchanged. That would cover the lookup, the deep copy and the `id` removal.

**Documentation:** `docs/omarchy-shell.md` and `agents/skills/shell-dev.md` list what the third-party facade provides but do not mention `entrySettings`. A sentence on it (a JSON snapshot of the plugin's own entry, `id` removed, refreshed on config change) would make it discoverable. The earlier note still applies: widgets hosted by a replacement bar get their facade from `pluginShellForBarEntry()`, which never sets `entrySettings`. Their `settings` property still carries the entry, so this matters only if `entrySettings` is meant for bar widgets too. If it is, it could be set there. If not, the exception could be documented.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `72eb616`, previously reviewed `70c62cb`, the base, current `quattro` and open #12996. Isolated headless Quickshell 0.3.1 runs used a model built from each source's verbatim host functions, including merges onto `quattro` and with #12996. The model used the real plugin registry, `AuthServiceStore.js`, `PluginShellApi.qml` and lock/polkit manifests, with stub service and overlay objects. It was not the full shell. No desktop session was run, `finishUnlock()` was not called, and the real polkit agent was not exercised. The PR's test script passed in a sandbox, where its compositor-dependent section was skipped.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
